# Mackay Regional Domain {.unnumbered}

*This chapter introduces the Mackay regional model — where it is and why it
matters, the modelling approach, and the simulation scenarios maintained in this
repository.*

## Location & setting

The model covers the **Pioneer River estuary at Mackay**, on the central
Queensland coast of Australia, together with the adjacent coastal waters of the
Coral Sea within the southern Great Barrier Reef lagoon. The Pioneer River
drains a predominantly sugarcane catchment of roughly 1,500 km² and discharges
through the city of Mackay to the sea.

Several features make this a demanding and interesting system to model:

- **Macro-tidal mouth.** Mackay experiences one of the largest tidal ranges on
  the Australian east coast — spring ranges of around 6 m — so the estuary is
  strongly tide-dominated and the mouth exchanges large volumes each tide. (The
  boundary-forcing water levels span roughly 0.1–6.6 m, consistent with this
  range.)
- **Episodic, flood-driven freshwater.** The climate is tropical with a
  pronounced summer wet season, and river flow is highly episodic — long dry
  spells punctuated by large floods. The most recent major event was the
  **January 2023 Mackay flood**, when the Pioneer River peaked near
  2,600 m³ s⁻¹.
- **Catchment nutrient loads.** The cane catchment delivers nutrient and sediment
  loads to a receiving environment adjacent to the Great Barrier Reef, so the
  estuary's water quality and its exchange with the lagoon are a key management
  concern — and the motivation for coupling biogeochemistry to the hydrodynamics.

These characteristics — large tidal exchange at the mouth and sharp,
flood-driven inputs at the river — are exactly the terms a nutrient budget must
balance, and they shape the test scenarios described below.

## Domain & approach

The model represents the Pioneer River estuary (Mackay, Queensland) and its
adjacent coastal waters. The Pioneer River is the dominant freshwater input; it
enters the model as a point source at the Bureau of Meteorology gauge 125013A
(Dumbleton Pump Station) and drives the estuarine response during flow events.

The setup couples SCHISM hydrodynamics with AED biogeochemistry on a single
unstructured mesh. River inflows enter as point sources
([river forcing](../part2-model-setup/08-atmospheric-and-river-forcing.qmd)),
the open ocean boundary is tidally forced
([tidal forcing](../part2-model-setup/07-boundary-and-tidal-forcing.qmd)), the
atmosphere is forced from gridded `sflux` fields, and biogeochemistry is
configured through
[`aed.nml`](../part2-model-setup/09-aed-and-tracers.qmd). General conservative
tracers (`GEN`) are included for mass-balance testing.

## Simulation scenarios

The repository tracks a sequence of runs under `runs/`, each building on the
previous one. They are recorded in `runs/RUN_LOG.md` and described in full in
[the run log chapter](../part5-running-the-model/20-run-scenarios-and-log.qmd).

| ID | Name | Purpose |
|----|------|---------|
| 001 | Pioneer_17 | Original baseline setup (archived, not in this repo). |
| 002 | `002_P18_flood` | Pioneer 18 with an **artificial flood pulse** and a simplified `fluxflag.prop` to enable deep testing of the boundary-flux budget. |
| 003 | `003_P18_flood_flat` | Copy of 002 with the flood pulse and a **quiescent (flat) ocean tide for the first 14 days**, to isolate flux-direction inconsistencies across the Pioneer mouth. |

Each run directory holds only the essential input/config files; outputs are
regenerated and are not stored in the repository.

## Why these scenarios

The flood pulse and the flat-tide variant exist to support a specific
investigation: a nutrient mass balance over the estuary would not close, and the
two candidate causes — mass loss at the high-rate river source, and untracked
transport across the tidal mouth — were entangled. Run 003 holds the tide flat
for two weeks so the source behaviour can be examined without tidal exchange,
then restores the full tide. The budget work is the subject of
[Part 4](../part4-nutrient-budget/14-budget-framework.qmd).
